{"self_assessment": "Impact
I laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line of the fish, from the nose over the back to the crossing. That is roughly half the outline, and it is the stroke the whole fall runs through. Before the push, the start connected to all 112 standing dominoes, nose to both tail tips. I also fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin early on, so nobody on the table was waiting for dominoes.

Execution
I worked steadily in small batches, tracing the back line continuously from the nose to the crossing. When the crossing needed a smoother sweep, I inspected the back line twice, closely, to look for weak points. I handed the last stretch from the crossing to the lower tail tip to Maya so that stretch got done quickly. I then stayed clear of that area to avoid bumps. After that I kept my hands off the finished run, because a bump was the main remaining risk.

Collaboration
I kept the table informed at each stage: when I was fetching, when I was tracing, when I was clear of the tail, and when it was time to stop touching things. I coordinated with Leo near the nose so our lines did not interfere. I accepted Maya's offer to take the tail stretch, and I worked with Tom and Maya on keeping the bin stocked.

Leadership
I backed Leo's fish idea straight away so we could start building. I took ownership of stroke 1 and made the timing and handoffs clear. I called the hands-off discipline at five minutes and again at two minutes, and I kept the mood light and the team focused through the final countdown.", "my_share_percent": 30}
